shared_inheritance_and_whitelist_rule.claim:
For Node1/Node2, Node2's instances receive Node1's applicable:

- Relation cardinalities.
- Declared Properties.
- Property Formats and value domains.
- Direct-value and nested-Property cardinalities.

Applicable local Node constraints also apply. Inheritance does not copy actual values or Relation facts. Reuse an inherited Property's Declaration; an inherited lookup creates no new Property or bearer.

MODEL inheritance is separate from Node narrowing. An explicit local MODEL override replaces the matching inherited effective rule in that MODEL. Unchanged inherited Declarations are reused. This does not modify the base MODEL or require duplicate effective owners.

Each Node's effective Declaration resolves its complete Relation whitelist, including permissions, directions, endpoints and cardinalities. A Relation absent from that effective whitelist is forbidden. An unresolved whitelist does not grant permission.

In Subject addresses and Formal Claims, `X/Y` selects a narrower Primary Node and `X//Name` an instance of a Primary Node. A Property cannot narrow or instantiate. `X.p` addresses a Property borne by X; an unchanged inherited Property is resolved to its existing declaration rather than redeclared or given another bearer. In Subject addresses, `X/(.p := V)` admits V as a Property value and selects the whole Primary Node X where p equals V. The case does not exclude other allowed values from X.p. `(Node, Node/**, .**)` selects the Node root and its declared branch; it is not a narrowing assertion.

`Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one composition fact, not narrowing. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite views of one classification fact. `:` marks an allowed value. `=` tests a condition; `==` establishes a required or derived conclusion. Parentheses group expressions; `in (a, b)` expresses membership. `@X` refers to the existing target without copying or reparenting it.

For `Source {:f}((RELATION)){:r} Target`, the pre-operator cardinality constrains the allowed number of outgoing Relation instances per selected source, and the post-operator cardinality constrains the allowed number of reverse links per selected target; reversal swaps their positions. The same notation constrains Properties, instances, and Relations. `{:n}` declares an allowed cardinality, not an actual value; `{=n}` tests a cardinality, and `{==n}` states a required conclusion. Repeated references in a rule, including its conditions and conclusions and both Step alternatives, bind the same selected member. An omitted cardinality annotation leaves that cardinality undefined, as in Current CA-R-2243; it is not an implicit zero or permission. Omitted-domain behavior requires a separate decision before parser adoption.

Subjects remain addresses and do not contain complete Formal Claims. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, including `Atom.Status := Draft` and `Atom/(.Role := Method)`; it does not write an instance value. Formal Claims retain separate `:` and `=` meanings. The withdrawn `..` form is not adopted; `::` has no assigned meaning here.

Evaluate ownership within the selected effective MODEL. Each member selected by (Node, Node/**, .**), including the root and each Property, has exactly one effective Current authoritative Requirement/Form: Declaration addressing that Node.

Count inherited Current Declarations and explicit local replacements after MODEL override resolution. A replaced base Declaration remains available in its base MODEL and is not a second effective owner in the local MODEL. Drafts and archives are not Current owners. Other Atoms may address the same Node.

```CFEL
Atom/(.Role: Requirement)/(.Form: Declaration)// ((HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT)){:1} (Node, Node/**, .**)
```

The count uses only the effective Current Declaration-to-Node links in that MODEL. HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT is derived from the dedicated Subject field. Each complete Current Atom's single Active Subject is governed by Atom.Subjects.Active.

Register status itself says relation-whitelist review remains.
genuine_gaps.consequence: For a listed Relation, report its explicit constraint. For an unlisted Relation, report no grant/unresolved whitelist; do not silently call it explicit zero or allowed.

genuine_gaps.consequence: A zero IS_PROPERTY_OF count closes only that Relation in the stated scope; it does not determine HAS_CLASSIFICATION, IS_CONTAINED_BY, RUN, INSTANCE_OF, or any other Relation.

genuine_gaps.gap: Container classification is not a child permission
genuine_gaps.evidence: HAS_CLASSIFICATION / `>| (Container == yes)` marks a target as Container. IS_CONTAINED_BY definition allows a Node target classified Container, but no generic all-child grant is declared by Container classification.
genuine_gaps.consequence: Scope Unit, Package, Project, Journal, MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE classify as Container where stated, but each has only its explicit contained-child relation permissions; do not infer arbitrary children.

genuine_gaps.gap: Relation endpoint definitions do not grant Primary edges
genuine_gaps.evidence: IS_PROPERTY_OF, NARROWER_THAN, INSTANCE_OF, IS_CONTAINED_BY, RUN, HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT, HAS_CLASSIFICATION, HAS_INVERSE, and HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR definitions describe relation direction/endpoints/inverses; they do not assert a relation instance for every matching pair.
genuine_gaps.consequence: Use per-Primary CFEL relation constraints to identify direct permissions. In particular, Event Record → Actor HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR has a defined endpoint signature but no Primary Declaration grant in this packet.
